One company hit the 1000 collection limit after a year of collection-per-repo and had to migrate to payload partitioning. Use a shared collection with a tenant key. "Isolated" tenant queries — each tenant only ever sees its own data, with good performance — is the default outcome of payload filtering (istenant=true) in a single shared collection. It does not require separate collections. Separate collections only apply to the legal/compliance case, not as a way to get isolation. readme_snippet: Auth And Authorization Auth is two systems, not one. Authentication identifies the caller. Authorization decides what the caller can touch. Conflating them ships flaws like "anyone with a valid token is admin" or "the route guard passed so the data layer trusts the body". The Discipline For any change that touches auth, answer five questions: AuthN: how does the system know who is calling, and what does it trust to know that. Cookie? Bearer token? Mutual TLS? Signed request? AuthZ: what is this principal allowed to do, on which resources, in which scope (tenant, project, row). Enforcement point: middleware, service, data layer (RLS), or several. Pick on purpose. Failure mode: closed by default. A missing rule denies, never allows. Auditability: every auth-relevant decision logs principal, scope, outcome, and trace ID. If any of those are vague, you are about to ship a hole.

readme_snippet: Boring By Default Complexity compounds. Novelty depreciates. The job is not to pick the technology you would enjoy operating, it is to pick the technology your on-call self at 3am will thank you for. The Discipline Before adopting a new piece of infrastructure (database, broker, language, framework, deployment model, auth library), answer in writing: What problem do we have that the current stack cannot solve? Specifically. With numbers if possible. What is the cheapest extension of the current stack that solves it? Often a column, an index, a job, or a config. What does this new thing cost us over five years? Operationally: backups, upgrades, on-call expertise, hiring, runbooks, monitoring. Who runs it at 3am? If the answer is "we will figure it out", the answer is no. If the new thing wins all four questions, adopt it. Most of the time it does not. The Default Stack Opinionated, defensible, dull. Deviations are justified, not free.
